title: TelemetryEvent
description: A single structured telemetry event emitted by a worker or orchestrator component during automation execution. Events must NOT contain secrets, authentication headers, cookies, or sensitive business payloads; redaction is the emitter's responsibility.

eventId.description: Unique identifier for this event instance. Must be globally unique (e.g. a UUID).

correlationId.description: Correlation identifier linking this event to a run, attempt, or causal chain. Used for distributed tracing.

eventType.description: The type of lifecycle event being recorded.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp at which the event occurred.

businessJobId.description: The business-layer job identifier, if applicable. May be null for infrastructure-only events.

leaseId.description: The lease identifier associated with this event, if applicable.

runId.description: The run identifier associated with this event, if applicable.

attemptId.description: The attempt identifier associated with this event, if applicable.

stepId.description: The step identifier associated with this event. Present for StepStarted and StepCompleted events.

workerId.description: The stable unique identity of the worker that emitted or is the subject of this event.

runState.description: The run state at the time of this event, if applicable.

stepState.description: The step state at the time of this event. Present for step-scoped events.

errorCategory.description: Error category if this event records a failure condition.

errorDetail.description: Stable error detail code (e.g. 'action.executionTimeout', 'action.commitUncertain', 'variable.uninitializedRead'). Must not contain sensitive data.

durationMs.description: Duration in milliseconds relevant to this event (e.g. step execution time, run total time). Must be measured with a monotonic clock per REF-10.

metadata.description: Must NOT contain secrets, authentication headers, cookies, or sensitive business payloads. Redaction is the emitter's responsibility. Use for diagnostic or operational data only (e.g. worker version, host class, retry count).
